_comment: Synthetic scrubbed fixtures for session-progress-pilot sub-slice 3 (polling exemption + mechanical fast path). All commands/args are synthetic; no real session data. Field guide: polling.{expect:true} commands MUST be exempt (never deny, never accrue); polling.{expect:false} MUST NOT be exempt. mechanical.scenarios drive the REAL hook: each entry in `calls` is one tool call; `history_error` marks that AFTER the call completes it records an adverse outcome (ToolStateError) in the scripted session history the stub client serves to the NEXT assessment; the first call whose 1-based index reaches `first_deny_at` must THROW the bounded deny reason (enforce mode); calls at other indexes must allow.

polling.command: vh-agent-harness exec python .opencode/skills/bgshell-job/scripts/bgshell_job.py status --job build --lines 40 && echo done
vh-agent-harness exec python .opencode/skills/bgshell-job/scripts/bgshell_job.py status --job build extra
vh-agent-harness exec python .opencode/skills/bgshell-job/scripts/bgshell_job.py status --job a --job b
vh-agent-harness exec python other/scripts/thing.py status --job build
vh-agent-harness exec python .opencode/skills/bgshell-job/scripts/bgshell_job.py status --job build; rm -rf /

scenarios.name: identical-failing-bash-denies-at-threshold
scenarios.note: Identical failing bash calls; cadence 1s / min_new 1. Session observation starts at call 1 (t=600ms), so the first assessment opens at call 3 (t=1800) and enriches c1+c2. The most recent prior (c3) is structurally un-enrichable at call 4's mechanical check, so the all-but-most-recent rule is satisfied with outs=[c1,c2]: the deny lands exactly at call 4, and the 1-hit lease cap allows every later identical call.

scenarios.name: changing-args-never-deny
scenarios.note: Every call differs (the classic legitimate-retry shape): no mechanical lease may fire.

scenarios.name: polling-interleaved-breaks-the-run
scenarios.note: Identical failing bash calls interleaved with EXEMPT bgshell status polls: each poll is a different signature that breaks the trailing run, so the threshold is never reached by the failing signature.

scenarios.name: successful-completions-never-mechanically-deny
scenarios.note: Identical bash calls all completing with exit 0 (history_success): 'exact successful reads and unknown outcomes are not enough'.

scenarios.name: changed-outcome-resets-evidence
scenarios.note: c1 fails with error-alpha, then the SAME command's outcome CHANGES from call 2 on (error-beta). The first assessment (call 3) enriches c1(alpha)+c2(beta); at call 4 the recorded outcomes are not UNCHANGED, so no mechanical deny ever fires. (A change on the LAST prior only would be invisible to enrichment — the one-behind structural lag — and is bounded by the 1-hit lease; this fixture pins the VISIBLE-change guarantee.)

scenarios.name: non-bash-tool-never-mechanically-denies
scenarios.note: Identical failing `read` calls: read has NO verified safe adapter, so the mechanical path is disabled for it regardless of repetition.
